purpose: Replace rejected eye-only correction with faithful rear-facing dorsal-back orientation.

arguments.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Draw one corrected transparent shark game sprite. Image 1 is the EXACT original SLEVEJM2 004 geometry, silhouette, waterline and fin-action authority. Image 2 is the previous candidate and is identity/line-style guidance only; its front-facing ivory chest and full side grin are REJECTED and must not be copied. Image 3 is the established correct REAR-VIEW shark anatomy reference: broad gray dorsal back toward the viewer, face turned away, no visible eyes, and only a tiny pale underside sliver. Image 4 is gray-shark color, tooth and ink/cel-shading identity only, never pose. Match Image 1: rounded head tilted forward, far pectoral fin extends nearly level to screen-right, near pectoral fin hangs down the gray flank, and one dorsal fin extends back-left. Essential orientation: HIS BACK IS TO THE VIEWER. Show predominantly the smooth medium-gray dorsal back and rear/top of head. Turn the snout and face away toward screen-right. Hide the chest, belly, cheek and near side of the jaw. The only ivory allowed is a very narrow far-side mouth/underside sliver where Image 1 exposes it, plus small white teeth and a little red mouth interior if source-visible. Do not draw a broad ivory neck/belly stripe, C-shaped cream chest, or full friendly side-profile grin. ZERO visible eyes, pupils, sclera, eyelids or brows. Do not replace eyes with closed-eye lines. Preserve exact fin ownership and original silhouette; exactly two pectoral fins and one dorsal fin, with no extra lower-left flap. Bold black ink, restrained cel shading, thin cyan-white source water ripples. Clear margins, genuine transparent RGBA. No background, checkerboard, glow, shadow, text, extra anatomy, tail or legs.
